pets.title: Wanting her buni's garden again, for the children and for herself
pets.description: The village and England meeting in a smell under her fork, and a summer like hers wanted for the children

pets.title: The village and England touching under her fork
pets.description: Nearly crying at the smell of the earth, a childhood garden gone wild, two countries meeting for a second

pets.title: A summer like hers for the children, whatever her mother thinks
pets.description: Knowing food by being there, tomatoes from the village on the list, and digging as going backwards

pets.title: “Slightly mad” to take a full plot she must prove she can keep
pets.description: Taking too much as she always does, strict to keep up, and one more thing to show the people who look at her

pets.title: Taking too much, as always, and strict to keep up
pets.description: A full plot before she could think, rules on the kitchen calendar, good at hard and not at slow

pets.title: Proving herself again, to an old man with a hat
pets.description: Judged a young mother with big ideas, after a life here of showing people

pets.title: “One thing that is mine”: a place to rest from being for others
pets.description: Wanting something not for anybody, a deckchair pictured, a rest like her buni's, and a good tired remembered

pets.title: Nobody to be for at the plot
pets.description: One thing of her own, and nobody there to reassure

pets.title: A rest she has forgotten how to take
pets.description: A deckchair she does not believe in, sitting like her buni, a good day with nothing planted, and a warm tired

T1:3:0.text: Taking a full plot before she could think, half laughing at herself
quotes: "Excited. And a bit mad, I think. Slightly mad. … And I said no, full. I don't know why I said this. It came out of my mouth before I think."
notes: Full, not half: the yes before thinking. Her mother's laugh down the phone from the village.

T1:5:0.text: Unsure yet what digging means for her, unlike her mother
quotes: "But after, a little bit, it stayed with me. … For her, to dig is going backwards. … But for me it's not backwards. For me it's, I don't know yet what it is. Something."
notes: Digging as going backwards for a mother who worked so she would not have to. 'Something': no word for it yet.

T1:7:0.text: Wanting the children to know food as she knew it at her buni's
quotes: "I want my kids to know where food comes from. … Nobody taught me. I just knew, because I was there. I want them to have one summer like this. Even small. Even in England."
notes: Carrots from a bag. Knowing by being there, not by being taught.

T1:9:0.text: A childhood garden alive in a smell, and gone wild now
quotes: "And the smell of the tomato leaves on your fingers, you know this smell? Green, a bit bitter. When I smell it now I am nine years old. … but the garden is gone wild because she can't do it any more."
notes: Nine years old in a smell. Buni ninety-one, the garden gone wild, three years since she went back.

T1:11:0.text: Nearly crying at the smell of turned earth: there and here at once
quotes: "the smell came up. Earth smell, wet. And I nearly cried. … Like I was there and here at the same time. In the village and in England."
notes: 'Stupid. Is not stupid, I know.' Corrects herself. A biscuit in the mud and she is back in England.

T1:13:0.text: Glad and hurt when her two countries meet
quotes: "You have two places, and most of the time they are far apart. … And for one second on the plot, with the smell, they were not far. … Good, and also it hurts a little."
notes: Romanian to the children, English back. The same clock on the wall since she was a baby. Good, and it hurts.

T1:15:0.text: Wanting one thing of her own, when all else is for others
quotes: "I wanted one thing that is mine. Everything is for somebody. … And I thought, I want one thing that is mine, even if it's mostly mud."
"I picture it. Me in a deckchair, with a book, in the sun … I know this is not how it will be. I know. But this is the picture in my head."
notes: 'Even if it's mostly mud.' The deckchair is a picture she does not believe in and keeps anyway.

T1:15:1.text: A deckchair she pictures but does not believe in
quotes: "I wanted one thing that is mine. Everything is for somebody. … And I thought, I want one thing that is mine, even if it's mostly mud."
"I picture it. Me in a deckchair, with a book, in the sun … I know this is not how it will be. I know. But this is the picture in my head."
notes: 'Even if it's mostly mud.' The deckchair is a picture she does not believe in and keeps anyway.

T1:17:0.text: Hoping for nobody to reassure at the plot
quotes: "But all day I make other people feel okay. … Nobody says it to me. Is not a complaint. Is just, I thought, on the plot nobody needs me to say anything."
notes: Nearly finished, you're doing great: said all day, never to her. The plot as a place with no one to reassure?

T1:19:0.text: A good day with nothing planted
quotes: "So we planted nothing. Nothing at all. But they were so happy. Muddy to the eyes, both. … So it was a good day, for nothing planted."
notes: Domnul Frog. Nothing planted and a good day all the same.

T1:21:0.text: Ambition on paper: a farm, her buni's tomatoes first
quotes: "Tomatoes, of course. Like my buni's … I asked my mother to send seeds from the village … I wrote a list. Is a long list. Chris read it and he said, Nell, this is a farm."
notes: Tomatoes like her buni's first on the list. Chris: 'this is a farm'. Taking too much again?

T1:23:0.text: Seen through by Chris when she promises time
quotes: "And I say, I'll find the time. And he makes this face. He has a face for when I say I'll find the time. He has seen this many times, I think. He knows me."
notes: Chris's face for 'I'll find the time'. Known, and a little caught out.

T1:25:0.text: Strict rules against a jungle by June
quotes: "I will have to be strict with myself. Very strict. I know how it is, if I let it slide in April, I will have a jungle by June. … So I have a plan. Two mornings a week, minimum"
notes: The calendar in the kitchen. A plan made against her own habits.

T1:27:0.text: Strictness learned to survive here: good at hard, not slow
quotes: "Nobody gives you anything here, you have to be strict, or you are nothing. So I am good at strict. I'm good at hard. … What I'm not so good at is slow."
notes: One suitcase, offices at night. 'Strict, or you are nothing.' Hard she can do, slow she cannot.

T1:31:0.text: Longing to sit as her buni sat
quotes: "She just sits, with her hands in her lap, and looks at the garden. … Now I think she was, I don't know the word, full. … But I would like to sit like her, one time, on my plot."
notes: 'Full': her word for her buni at rest. She has never sat like that.

T1:33:0.text: Judged by a look at the pushchair, a young mother with big ideas
quotes: "he looked at my pushchair like, what is this woman doing here with a baby. … He thinks I'm one more young mother with big ideas. … But I want to show him."
notes: The man with the hat. A look, nothing said, heard as a verdict.

T1:35:0.text: The plot one more thing to prove here
quotes: "But all my life here, I have to show people. Show them I speak English properly, show them I'm not here to take something … The plot will be one more thing I show them."
notes: Showing people all her life here. The patient who asked for the English nurse.

T1:37:0.text: Afraid the plot will show she took too much again
quotes: "That I took too much. That's always my problem. … So if the plot is a jungle in June, it means I did it again. I took too much. But I want to try."
notes: 'I take too much', said by Chris and her mother too. Wants to try anyway.

T1:39:0.text: Remembering a good tired after years of grey
quotes: "But it was a good tired. Not the tired from work, from standing, from the commute, that tired is grey. This was a good tired, warm. … I forgot there is a good tired."
notes: Grey tired and warm tired. Six years of the grey kind.

pets.title: A guest in her mother's half, “grateful and small”
pets.description: Her mother clearing in three weeks what she could not in three months, a garden she chose to leave, and Nell grateful and small

pets.title: Shamed by a letter, and hiding from the plot holders
pets.description: Her name written down, a blameless record spoiled over vegetables, and early mornings at the far fence

pets.title: Awake to being behind, and not one to give it back
pets.description: Seeing only what is undone, racing the weeds, the good tired gone, and still not one to give things back

pets.title: The help on her son's plot
pets.description: Kept on for him, his sunflowers exactly what she wanted, the mess hers alone to see, and her own deckchair never opened

T2:3:0.text: Coming home from the plot worse than she went
quotes: "And every time I go to the plot I see only what I have not done. … And I come home feeling worse than before I went. Is crazy. I go there to feel better and I come home worse."
notes: 'I am very good at predicting myself.' The calendar looks back at her. Goes to feel better, comes home worse.

T2:5:0.text: Too pressed by the jungle to look at the children
quotes: "I just pull, pull, pull, the weeds by the path, fast, like I'm racing somebody. … Matei is shouting mama look, mama look, and I say yes, beautiful, without looking."
notes: Racing somebody, but who? 'Yes, beautiful, without looking.'

T2:7:0.text: Feeling watched and found wanting by the other plot holders
quotes: "Like walking into a room where everybody knows you did something wrong. … Maybe they don't look. Maybe they don't care at all. But I feel it on my back, like a hand."
notes: Mine 'like the house of somebody who died'. Unsure anyone looks, sure she feels it.

T2:9:0.text: Shamed to tears by the committee letter
quotes: "I read it in the car, outside the nursery, and I cried. … Like somebody walked past my plot with a clipboard and wrote my name down."
notes: A letter with a logo. Daria in the back: is it the radio. Somebody wrote her name down.

T2:11:0.text: A blameless record here spoiled by a letter about vegetables
quotes: "I always pay first, I always fill the forms correct, I always do everything they ask. Eleven years in this country and I never get one letter like this. And now for vegetables."
"But I don't give things back. I'm not a person who gives things back. If I give back every hard thing, I would be in the village still."
notes: Eleven years of forms filled correct. 'Like a schoolgirl': apologising for her children.

T2:11:1.text: Not one to give hard things back
quotes: "I always pay first, I always fill the forms correct, I always do everything they ask. Eleven years in this country and I never get one letter like this. And now for vegetables."
"But I don't give things back. I'm not a person who gives things back. If I give back every hard thing, I would be in the village still."
notes: Eleven years of forms filled correct. 'Like a schoolgirl': apologising for her children.

T2:13:0.text: Hiding from the other plot holders since the letter
quotes: "I'm hiding, I know this. I'm a grown woman hiding from pensioners with clipboards. But I can't help it."
notes: Half past six, Thursday evenings, the far fence. Pretending to do something important with the onions.

T2:15:0.text: Sunflowers taller than her son: exactly what she wanted
quotes: "Every Sunday he stands next to them and I take a photo, and he says mama, measure me … That part is exactly what I wanted. Exactly."
notes: 'Mama, measure me.' The one part exactly as pictured.

T2:19:0.text: Lonely in seeing the mess so the children need not
quotes: "But lonely because I am the only one who sees it. … This is being a mother, I think, a lot of the time. Seeing the mess so they don't have to."
notes: A mother at a party seeing the mess. Lonely in what she alone sees.

T2:21:0.text: Even her free hour spent on guilt
quotes: "The deckchair is still in the shed. Folded. … Even the guilt is not mine. Even the guilt is for the plot. I wanted one thing that is mine and now I have one more thing that I'm failing at."
notes: Striped, bought in April, never opened. Even her guilt belongs to the plot.

T2:23:0.text: Kept on only for her son, herself the help
quotes: "And I cannot say to him we're not going any more. I cannot do this. So I suppose it's his now, really. The plot is his and I am the help."
notes: Sunday night: give it up. Monday morning: his question. She cannot say no to him.

T2:27:0.text: Outdone in three weeks by her mother
quotes: "And in three weeks she cleared half of it. Half. … In three weeks she did what I didn't do in three months. And she didn't laugh at me this time."
notes: No laugh this time from her mother. 'She just worked.'

T2:29:0.text: A minute in her buni's garden, then a guest on her own plot
quotes: "it looked like my buni's garden. … And for one minute I was so happy. Like I opened a door and the village was there. And then the next minute I felt like a visitor. … I was standing on my own plot like a guest."
notes: A door opening on the village, then a guest. The girl with the bucket again.

T2:31:0.text: Praised for her mother's work: grateful and small
quotes: "The secretary walked past and he said, well done, Nell, what a difference. To me! … Small. Grateful and small at the same time."
notes: Praised for her mother's work. No word for it in either language: grateful and small.

T2:33:0.text: Struck that her mother remade here the garden she chose to leave
quotes: "And she left it. She chose to leave it. And now she comes to England and makes it again on my plot, in three weeks, like she never left."
notes: Buni talked to the peppers. Her mother chose to leave the garden, and made it again here.

T2:35:0.text: Grateful for a kitchen smelling of home
quotes: "But the dill, I cook with her dill now, I put it in the soup, and the whole kitchen smells like home. Like my buni's kitchen. So I am grateful. I am. Even when I'm small, I'm grateful."
notes: Two halves, two women, 'hers is good'. The dill in the soup smells like buni's kitchen.

T2:37:0.text: The good tired gone: the plot one more grey thing
quotes: "My body says no and I go anyway. … Now there is no good tired. Is just tired. The grey one. The plot became one more grey thing."
notes: 'In March I told you there is a good tired.' Holds herself to what she said.

T2:39:0.text: Behind with everything, and most visibly at the plot
quotes: "Behind is my whole body. I wake up already behind. … And instead it's the place where I'm most behind of all, where you can see how behind I am, with your eyes, in weeds."
notes: Behind with phoning her buni too. The plot shows it 'with your eyes, in weeds'.

T2:41:0.text: Woken from a dream of the plot, not sure she likes it
quotes: "I think in March I was a bit, dreaming. … Now I'm awake. Is not bad, to be awake. … I don't know yet if I like what it is. But at least I see it."
notes: Dreaming in March, awake now. Not sure she likes it, glad to see it.

pets.title: Letting go of her buni's garden, which “you cannot dig”
pets.description: Giving away her mother's half, where she was a guest, and finding she wanted her buni's garden itself, not a plot

pets.title: Giving away the guest's half, and a little grief
pets.description: Her mother's half let go, another's leeks where the dill was, and leaving felt even here

pets.title: Her buni's garden, not a plot, and nothing digging finds
pets.description: Back in her buni's garden the wish all along, her buni glad she tried, and the village tomatoes in a drawer

pets.title: Half given away: failed, relieved, a little less strict
pets.description: Proof she took too much, a morning free of the plot, her mother's laugh heard anew, and slow learned a little

pets.title: Failure and relief at once, and her mother's laugh heard anew
pets.description: Too much again, a backpack taken off, and her mother laughing at the too much, not at her

pets.title: Learning a little slow, after a year of attacking the plot
pets.description: Less strict, the pottering a lie, and the good tired back for a day

pets.title: The feared judgement gone, its letter kept with her passports
pets.description: A pumpkin and a strawberry plant from those she thought had judged her, and the committee letter in with the passports

pets.title: Ten minutes of her own on the children's plot
pets.description: The deckchair opened once and left for weeding, on a plot no longer pretended to be her hobby, the children's place and glad of it

pets.title: Ten minutes of rest she could not keep
pets.description: The March picture for ten minutes, owing nothing like the spent sunflowers, then up and weeding

pets.title: The children's place, and glad of it
pets.description: The hobby no longer pretended, their pride in seeds and strawberries, a harvest got away with

T3:3:0.text: A harvest she got away with, much of it her mother's
quotes: "And courgettes, so many courgettes, from my mother's half. … And I think, we got away with it. That's how it feels."
notes: Nine strawberries, counted. 'We got away with it', said twice.

T3:7:0.text: Delighted by the children's pride in their sunflower seeds and strawberries
quotes: "he picked out every seed, one by one, a whole evening, and he put them in an envelope. And he wrote on it, Matei sunflowers next year."
notes: The s backwards on the envelope, on the fridge. Seven of the nine picked by Daria, four or five eaten.

T3:9:0.text: Giving up half: failure and relief unresolved
quotes: "I felt like I had failed. When I decided, I felt like I had failed. And then I felt relieved. Both. And I still don't know which one is right."
notes: Failed, then relieved, and 'maybe both are right'. Leaves it open.

T3:11:0.text: Failure as proof she took too much again
quotes: "Three times I wrote it and deleted it. Because I know what it means. It means the man with the hat was right. It means I took too much, again, like always, and I couldn't hold it."
"the next morning I woke up and the first thought in my head was not the plot. First time since March. … like when you take off a backpack you forgot you were carrying."
notes: Three drafts deleted. The man with the hat proved right in her head. Then rain as the first thought.

T3:11:1.text: Relief: a morning when her first thought was not the plot
quotes: "Three times I wrote it and deleted it. Because I know what it means. It means the man with the hat was right. It means I took too much, again, like always, and I couldn't hold it."
"the next morning I woke up and the first thought in my head was not the plot. First time since March. … like when you take off a backpack you forgot you were carrying."
notes: Three drafts deleted. The man with the hat proved right in her head. Then rain as the first thought.

T3:13:0.text: A mother's laugh understood at last
quotes: "So she was not laughing at me. She was laughing at the too much. All year I thought she was laughing at me, at the village girl digging in England. … I didn't know it was different."
notes: The March laugh heard again: at the too much, not at her. A year's reading of her mother undone.

T3:15:0.text: Giving away the half where she was a guest
quotes: "I gave away the good half and I kept the half with the jungle and Matei's sunflowers. … Mama's half was never mine. It was beautiful, but it was never mine. I was a guest there."
notes: Chris: keep the good half. She keeps the jungle and the sunflowers. A guest's half is no half.

T3:17:0.text: Wanting her buni's garden all along, not a plot
quotes: "I wanted to be at my buni's again. Not to have a garden. To be in her garden. … And you cannot dig that. You can dig all day in England and you will not find it."
"And I said, buni, I didn't plant tomatoes. And she laughed more. She was happy that I'm trying. That was enough. That was more than enough."
notes: 'Is not in the soil.' Buni, ninety-two, asks after tomatoes never planted, and laughs.

T3:17:1.text: Enough that her buni was happy she tried
quotes: "I wanted to be at my buni's again. Not to have a garden. To be in her garden. … And you cannot dig that. You can dig all day in England and you will not find it."
"And I said, buni, I didn't plant tomatoes. And she laughed more. She was happy that I'm trying. That was enough. That was more than enough."
notes: 'Is not in the soil.' Buni, ninety-two, asks after tomatoes never planted, and laughs.

T3:19:0.text: The village tomatoes never started, perhaps for her son
quotes: "They're still in the envelope, in the kitchen drawer. Buni's tomatoes, from the village, in a drawer in England. … I think maybe they are his to plant, not mine."
notes: Seeds wrapped in newspaper, never the right day. 'His to plant, not mine.'

T3:21:0.text: No more pretending it is her hobby
quotes: "I have stopped pretending it's my hobby. … It's their place, and I'm glad they have one. Really glad."
notes: 'Every child should have a place like this.' The hobby dropped as a pretence.

T3:23:0.text: Attacking the plot and calling it pottering
quotes: "But I don't potter. I attack. I go to the plot like I go to a war. … Is the biggest lie of my year, the pottering."
notes: Potter: a word learned this year for a way she cannot be.

T3:25:0.text: The good tired back for a day
quotes: "I said no, I'm just not behind any more. And the good tired came back, one time … It came back for one day."
notes: A week of sleeping like the children. The good tired back, once.

T3:29:0.text: A little grief at leeks where the dill was
quotes: "Somebody else's curtains, where your life was. Like this. Malcolm's leeks where my mother's dill was, where my buni's garden was for three weeks. Is fine. It's only a little moment."
notes: Another's curtains in the window of an old flat.

quotes: "That's what it is to leave, I think. Everything you left keeps going without you. Is normal. But the plot, I didn't expect it there, in England."
notes: Her school a supermarket now. Leaving keeps happening, even here.

T3:33:0.text: Surprised by the kindness of those she felt watched by
quotes: "They are kind. Really kind. … He came in October and he gave Daria a strawberry plant in a pot. … So maybe they never thought I'm crazy. Maybe only I thought this."
notes: 'For the little gardener.' The man with the hat knows Daria's name.

T3:35:0.text: The committee letter kept with her passports, unable to laugh
quotes: "The important papers drawer. Birth certificates, passports, my qualification, the letter that says you can stay. And this one. … A paper that says something about me. … Chris laughed when he saw it there. I didn't laugh."
notes: Kept with the letter that says she can stay. Why there? 'Important, in a bad way.'

T3:37:0.text: Ten minutes in the deckchair, then unable to stay
quotes: "And I opened the deckchair. First time. … And I sat for ten minutes. Then I got up and I started weeding. I couldn't stay. I don't know how to sit."
notes: Mouldy from the shed, the March picture exactly, ten minutes long.

T3:39:0.text: Ten minutes owing nothing, like the spent sunflowers
quotes: "Ten minutes in a chair with nobody needing me, nobody behind me, no phone. … They're finished. They can stand there with their heads down and nobody shouts at them. … But for ten minutes I was like the sunflowers."
notes: Dead sunflowers with their heads down, finished, not shouted at.

T3:41:0.text: A little less strict with herself, learning slow
quotes: "Only that I think I'm less strict. With me, I mean. A little bit. … the garden doesn't care if you're strict, Nell. … I think I am learning a little bit of slow."
notes: Her buni: the garden does not read your calendar.
